module.title: Classes, Objects & Shared Refs
module.subtitle: How classes bundle state + methods, and why two variables can share one object
lesson_points: A class is a blueprint; calling Ship(...) builds an object instance in memory and runs __init__(self, ...).
Methods are functions attached to the class—'self' automatically refers to whichever object you called it on.
Assigning alias = hero_ship does NOT copy the object; both names point to the exact same object card in memory!

quizzes.title: Shared Object Aliasing
quizzes.prompt: What does hero.fuel print after alias.burn(15) runs?
quizzes.explanation: hero and alias point to the exact same Ship object in memory, so burning 15 via alias lowers hero.fuel to 35.

quizzes.title: Spot the Missing 'self'
quizzes.prompt: Click the line in burn() that creates a temporary local variable instead of updating the Ship object's field.
quizzes.explanation: Line 5 writes 'fuel = ...' (a local variable that vanishes on return) instead of 'self.fuel = ...'.

quizzes.title: Why Does Aliasing Surprise Devs?
quizzes.prompt: Why does modifying 'alias' in 'alias = hero' also change 'hero'?
quizzes.sample_explanation: Assigning alias = hero copies the reference pointing to the same Ship object in memory rather than making a separate copy.
quizzes.explanation: Python variables hold references to objects; mutating through one reference affects every variable sharing that object.
